title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
version: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as corrected (three corrigenda); amendments proposed in COM(2025) 501 and COM(2025) 837 not adopted per EUR-Lex
applicability: Binding law, but applies to Echelon only if Unbound processes personal data of people in the EU in the context of offering services to them or monitoring them (Art. 3(2)), or if a customer subject to GDPR engages Unbound as processor. DAF donors are predominantly US taxpayers; EU-resident donors to US DAFs are possible but not established. Rating: unlikely, conditional. Customers still ask GDPR-style questions by convention.
license: EU legal act published in the Official Journal. EUR-Lex content may be reused with acknowledgment under the Commission reuse policy (Decision 2011/833/EU); only the OJ edition is authentic.
limitations: Extraterritorial reach is fact-specific; no EU establishment for Echelon.
notes: Open question: will any Unbound sponsor knowingly serve EU-resident donors or grantees?

verification.method: Fetched EUR-Lex act page and ALL (document information) page 2026-11-25: only corrigenda listed under 'Modified by'; proposed amendments 52025PC0501 and 52025PC0837 listed.

license: UK legislation is Crown copyright, reusable under the Open Government Licence v3.0 (legislation.gov.uk standard terms; not re-read this pass).
limitations: Commencement of DUAA provisions is phased; check commencement regulations.

license: EU legal act published in the Official Journal. EUR-Lex content may be reused with acknowledgment under the Commission reuse policy (Decision 2011/833/EU); only the OJ edition is authentic. SCC text is meant to be incorporated without modification.

title: California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act (Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100 et seq.) and CPPA regulations (Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, div. 6)
issuer: California Legislature; California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA); California Attorney General
version: As amended; regulations updated by the CPPA package adopted 2025-07-24 (approved by OAL 2025-09-22, effective 2026-01-01)
applicability: Binding on 'businesses' (for-profit entities meeting thresholds). Most DAF sponsors are nonprofit public charities and are generally outside the 'business' definition, and Echelon is unlikely to meet the thresholds (revenue, 100,000 consumers, or majority revenue from selling or sharing). Unbound would be a 'service provider' only for customers that are CCPA businesses. Commercial affiliates of sponsors may be businesses, but GLBA-covered data is exempted at the data level. Rating: conditional, low-to-medium likelihood; confidence medium.
license: California statutes and regulations are public law; no reuse restriction.
limitations: Thresholds are inflation-adjusted; nonprofit and GLBA carve-outs are fact-specific.

verification.method: Fetched CPPA regulations pages and California AG CCPA page 2026-11-25; enactment date not re-verified.

title: CPPA regulations on CCPA updates, cybersecurity audits, risk assessments, automated decisionmaking technology (ADMT) and insurance
version: Final rulemaking package (Board adoption 2025-07-24; OAL approval 2025-09-22)
applicability: Binding on CCPA businesses. Adds risk assessments, annual cybersecurity audits and ADMT access and opt-out rights for covered businesses, with staged deadlines (not captured). Reaches Unbound only via CCPA-covered customers or if Echelon itself becomes a covered business; customers covered by it may push cybersecurity-audit evidence requests to service providers. Rating: conditional, low likelihood.
limitations: Phased compliance dates for audits and ADMT not captured in this pass.
notes: Newly discovered source (not in seed list). Open question: phased dates for cybersecurity audit and ADMT compliance.

verification.method: Fetched CPPA CCPA updates page 2026-11-25 (effective date 2026-01-01; rulemaking complete).

title: US state comprehensive consumer privacy laws (umbrella)
issuer: Various state legislatures; tracked by IAPP Westin Research Center
version: Umbrella; IAPP tracker last updated 2026-09-08 (count of enacted states not captured)
applicability: Binding in each enacting state on entities meeting that state's thresholds. Key nuance for Unbound: several state laws (for example Colorado, Oregon, Delaware, Minnesota and New Jersey, to be confirmed statute by statute) do not exempt nonprofits, so DAF sponsors and their processors may be covered where the CCPA would not cover them; most include GLBA exemptions that may be entity-level or data-level. Rating: conditional, medium likelihood for sponsors with large donor bases; confidence low until statute review.
license: Statutes are public law. The IAPP tracker is copyrighted IAPP content (member resource); cite, do not copy.
limitations: Umbrella record; each statute needs its own record before an answer relies on it. Nonprofit coverage list above is from prior knowledge and not verified in this pass.
notes: Open question: which enacted state laws cover nonprofit DAF sponsors and processors, and with what thresholds?

verification.method: Fetched IAPP tracker landing page 2026-11-25 (secondary source); no individual statute verified in this pass.

title: US state data breach notification laws (umbrella)
applicability: Binding. All US states have breach notification statutes (per NCSL, not re-verified this pass); most require a third party that maintains data on behalf of another entity to notify the data owner promptly. Applies to Unbound as a maintainer of donor personal information for sponsors. Rating: likely applicable; confidence high in principle, details per state.
license: Statutes are public law; NCSL compilations are NCSL copyright.
limitations: NCSL page returned HTTP 403. Definitions of personal information vary (some include account credentials, biometric data).

verification.method: Not verified: NCSL page blocked (HTTP 403); umbrella relies on prior knowledge.

title: Regulation P, Privacy of Consumer Financial Information (12 CFR part 1016)
applicability: Binds financial institutions under CFPB jurisdiction regarding privacy notices and sharing of nonpublic personal information (NPI). DAF sponsors are generally 501(c)(3) charities, and whether a sponsor is a GLBA 'financial institution' is not established. The affiliated bank or broker-dealer is covered; if it shares NPI with Unbound (for example account linkage), the reuse and redisclosure limits (12 CFR 1016.11) and service-provider exception (1016.13) would flow to Unbound by contract. Rating: indirect or contractual; confidence medium-low.
license: US federal government work; not subject to US copyright (17 U.S.C. 105). Free to reuse and quote with citation.
limitations: SEC-registered entities follow Regulation S-P instead (see financial-services register).
notes: Open question: is any target sponsor itself a GLBA financial institution, or only its commercial affiliate?

verification.method: eCFR versioner API for title 12 part 1016 2026-11-25 (latest amendment 2018-09-17); original publication date not re-verified.

Reuse and quotation permitted with citation; third-party material inside a publication may carry its own rights.
limitations: 1.1 is still a draft; avoid citing draft subcategory IDs as final.
notes: Version check: 1.1 remains a draft as of 2026-11-25.
